expected_effect: Direction: public_val_bpb decreases. Size: steps rise +8..18% vs same-host control (approx. 2240..2450 vs 2071/2076) and public_val_bpb falls by 0.002..0.006 (target < 1.0037 on trn21, < 1.0040 on trn22). If steps rise >= 3% but BPB is >= control, BF16 at the MLP input is judged to cost quality (FALSIFIED-QUALITY) and the global-policy regression is attributed at least partly to the MLP path; if steps stay within +/-2%, the boundary is not a measurable cost (FALSIFIED-INERT).
hypothesis: In the pinned default configuration the transformer Block feeds an FP32 norm(x) output into the MLP, so the MLP up/down projections run as FP32 matmuls. The ledger shows this class of boundary is the dominant per-step cost: the global --bf16-norm-output policy (all norm outputs BF16) reached 2716 steps vs 2071 (+31%) but regressed public_val_bpb to 1.016279, while the single isolated --bf16-sdpa-input boundary reached 2233 vs 2076 (+7.6%) and improved BPB to 1.002028 (KEEP). BF16 inputs to hidden-layer matmuls are standard mixed-precision practice; the plausible quality culprit in the global policy is the final norm -> lm_head/softcap-CE path (and/or other non-matmul norm sites), not the MLP. Casting exactly one tensor per Block -- the MLP-input norm output -- to BF16 should recover a large share of the step-rate gain (predicted +8..18% steps) while preserving per-step learning, lowering fixed-budget public_val_bpb. This is the narrowest untested precision boundary; the previous attempt (20260922-bf16-mlp-input-norm-only) PASSED proposal review and failed only implementation review because the parallel_block code path bypassed the toggle, which this revision specifies explicitly.
implementation_plan: All edits confined to train.py on branch autoloop/20260922-bf16-mlp-input-norm-r3 from 9a4caa7b. STEP 1 (static inspection, reported only as a note inside the implementation summary; no artifact file, no execution): (a) open norm() (around lines 1446-1462) and record the module-level constant implementing the --bf16-norm-output policy (GLOBAL) and confirm its cast target is torch.bfloat16; (b) open Block.forward and enumerate every norm() call and every code path: default serial path (parallel_block=False, mlp_sandwich=False): norm(q_in), norm(k_in), norm(v_in), the norm(x) feeding local_conv, and the norm(x) whose result is the argument of self.mlp(...); the mlp_sandwich variant and its MLP-input norm; the parallel_block variant (h = norm(x) shared by attention and self.mlp(h, fc=fc), early return) and how fc is produced when coalescing is 'none' versus a coalesced mode; record line numbers; (c) confirm that under default flags (GLOBAL False) the serial-path MLP-input norm output is FP32; if it is already BF16, stop and report HALT-INERT; (d) confirm MLP/Linear already accept BF16 input via the existing BF16 weight-cache path (no MLP-internal edit). STEP 2 (toggle): following the existing --bf16-sdpa-input pattern, add module-level USE_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT = True with env override NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT ('0' disables), argparse pair --bf16-mlp-norm-output / --no-bf16-mlp-norm-output (dest bf16_mlp_norm_output, default None -> constant), resolved in main() where bf16_norm_output / bf16_sdpa_input are resolved, and append 'USE_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT' to ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES (around lines 5251-5266) so current_toggles()/save_checkpoint() persist it and load_for_eval() restores it before model construction. Default must resolve True so the candidate run uses no flags. STEP 3 (site-scoped casts; do NOT modify norm(), Linear.forward, the MLP module, or the weight-cache logic): define the three-line pattern P as: bind the MLP-input tensor to a local (mlp_in), then `if USE_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT and mlp_in.dtype != torch.bfloat16: mlp_in = mlp_in.to(torch.bfloat16)`, then pass mlp_in to self.mlp exactly where the original tensor was passed. Apply P at: (3a) the default serial path: mlp_in = norm(x) at the existing MLP-input norm call, then self.mlp(mlp_in) in the same residual statement; if any op sits between that norm and self.mlp, cast immediately at the norm output and leave the intervening op untouched; (3b) the mlp_sandwich path: at its MLP-input norm call only (the post-MLP sandwich norm and everything else untouched); (3c) the parallel_block path: keep `h = norm(x)` and every attention use of h byte-for-byte unchanged; if this path calls self.mlp with h as the activation input and fc is None (coalescing 'none'), apply P with mlp_in = h (a cast copy; h itself is not modified, so attention inputs stay unchanged); if this path supplies the MLP a coalesced projection (fc is not None, or the up-projection is produced jointly with qkv from the shared h), do NOT insert any cast on that path and instead, in GPT.__init__ (or the Block constructor, once per model) print exactly one line 'bf16_mlp_norm_output: inapplicable under parallel_block coalesced projections; no cast applied' when USE_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT and parallel_block and par_coalesce != 'none'. Do NOT touch norm(q_in)/norm(k_in)/norm(v_in), the local_conv norm, rope_norm/QK norms, the GPT.forward initial norm, the final norm, lm_head, softcap/CE, eval, causality, optimizer, schedule, data or launch code. STEP 4 (logging): add exactly one field 'bf16_mlp_norm_output=<bool>' to the existing precision-options config oneliner printed at startup (the oneliner reporting bf16_norm_output / bf16_sdpa_input). STEP 5 (static self-review inside the implementation summary; no execution required): state that the diff is limited to the toggle/env/CLI resolution, the ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES entry, the pattern-P casts at the serial, sandwich and parallel(non-coalesced) MLP-input sites, the single inapplicability print for the coalesced parallel path, and the one log field; quote the line numbers of each modified site and of the untouched attention norms, local_conv norm, final norm and lm_head call; state that with NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT=0 the original code path executes on every path; state that under --bf16-norm-output the dtype guard makes the change a no-op; state that in the parallel path h remains the uncast tensor for attention; state that checkpoint format (one additional toggle name), eval code, optimizer, data and launch shape are otherwise unchanged; state num_params_M is unchanged (592.9). single_causal_change: One numerical-format boundary change confined to train.py: a new module-level toggle USE_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT (default True; env NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT='0' disables; CLI --bf16-mlp-norm-output/--no-bf16-mlp-norm-output; appended to ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES so checkpoints persist it and load_for_eval restores it) casts exactly ONE tensor per transformer Block to torch.bfloat16 (the identical cast target the existing --bf16-norm-output policy uses): the norm output that is the direct input of the MLP module. In the default serial path (parallel_block=False, mlp_sandwich=False, the path exercised by the candidate) this is the result of the norm(x) call passed to self.mlp(...). The cast is guarded by a dtype check so that under --bf16-norm-output (norm already returns BF16) behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged. For consistency of the toggle's meaning across Block.forward variants: (i) the mlp_sandwich path casts its own MLP-input norm output the same way (post-MLP sandwich norm untouched); (ii) the parallel_block path with non-coalesced projections keeps the shared h = norm(x) untouched for attention and passes a separately cast copy of h to self.mlp only; (iii) the parallel_block path with coalesced projections (where the MLP consumes a projection computed jointly with qkv from the shared h) is declared inapplicable: no cast is applied and one explicit startup line is printed. Acknowledged downstream propagation: MLP up-projection/activation/down-projection run on BF16 activations via the already-exercised BF16-input Linear path (Linear.forward selects the weight cache matching input dtype), and the MLP output is added to the FP32 residual with the existing promotion semantics -- the same consumer path the --bf16-norm-output full run exercised end-to-end. NOT changed: norm(q_in)/norm(k_in)/norm(v_in), the norm feeding local_conv, QK norms/rope_norm, the GPT.forward initial embedding norm, the final norm before lm_head, lm_head, logits/softcap/CE, ngram-ve, optimizer, schedule, batch, data, eval, causality, launch shape or environment. num_params_M must remain 592.9 and every existing config oneliner must be identical to the control except for one added field. Launch smoke and full with the exact control command/environment and no additional flags. Full-run classification vs same-host pinned control (trn21 2071 / 1.005734; trn22 2076 / 1.005967), evaluated in order: (1) HALT-INERT if static inspection finds the MLP-input norm output is already BF16 under default flags (no patch, no run); (2) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if full-run steps < 90% of same-host control (<1864 trn21, <1869 trn22); (3) FALSIFIED-INERT if steps within +/-2% of control (the MLP-input FP32 boundary is not a measurable cost); (4) SUCCESS if steps >= +3% of control and public_val_bpb < same-host control by >= 0.002; (5) FALSIFIED-QUALITY if steps >= +3% and public_val_bpb >= control (BF16 at the MLP input costs more quality than the extra steps buy); (6) INCONCLUSIVE otherwise (+2..3% steps, or >= +3% with a gain smaller than 0.002). Verdicts use only fixed-budget public_val_bpb; the Analyst records as attribution notes only (not verdict inputs) the fraction of steps beyond the ~2195-step data wall documented in train.py and the smoothed training-loss log value at the control's final step count.
